technique.how: With the patient sitting, leaning forward, in full expiration, listen with the diaphragm at the left lower sternal border and right upper sternal border for a high-pitched, blowing, decrescendo early-diastolic murmur. Compare with prior documented examinations and note associated wide pulse pressure or collapsing pulse.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet environment; knowledge of whether a murmur was previously documented (a 'new' murmur requires a baseline).

interpretation.positive_finding: In suspected dissection a diastolic murmur is present in only about a quarter of cases and raises the probability only slightly (LR+ about 1.4); in fever/bacteraemia a new regurgitant murmur is a minor Duke criterion for endocarditis and should prompt blood cultures and echocardiography.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of a diastolic murmur does not lower the probability of aortic dissection meaningfully (about 72% of dissections have no murmur) and does not exclude endocarditis.
interpretation.pitfalls: Soft early-diastolic murmurs are easily missed in a noisy ED or tachycardic patient, and a chronic AR murmur in a patient without a baseline exam may be mislabelled as new. Interobserver agreement for soft murmurs is poor (unverified recall).
interpretation.changes_what: Present in chest pain: adds little on its own but with pulse deficit/neurologic deficit go straight to CT angiography; absent: does not lower dissection probability - image if the story fits.

estimates.population: Pooled from 21 studies of >=18 consecutive patients with confirmed thoracic aortic dissection (1966-2000 literature); LR derived within the review from studies with controls
estimates.reference_standard: Confirmed dissection by imaging, surgery or autopsy as defined in the included studies
estimates.quote: Presence of a diastolic murmur does little to change the pretest probability of dissection (positive LR, 1.4; 95% CI, 1.0-2.0)

sources.citation: Klompas M. Does this patient have an acute thoracic aortic dissection? JAMA. 2002.
Ohle R, Kareemi HK, Wells G, Perry JJ. Clinical Examination for Acute Aortic Dissection: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2018.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of a murmur to exclude dissection or endocarditis; do not treat a murmur as 'new' without a documented baseline.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: New AR murmur with tearing chest pain, pulse deficit or neurologic deficit = presumed type A dissection: emergent CT angiography and cardiothoracic surgery; with fever and bacteraemia = urgent echocardiography for endocarditis.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver reliability estimate located in the sources retrieved.

extraction_notes: Klompas 2002 abstract gives pooled sensitivity '28% have a diastolic murmur' (Abstract, Results) and LR+ 1.4 (1.0-2.0) but no specificity or LR-, so the record is partially_quantified (no sens/spec or LR pair). Ohle 2018 (PubMed lists 2018; journal issue 2019) abstract does not report a murmur estimate and the full text is not open access, so no second estimate could be quoted. Search 'diastolic murmur aortic dissection sensitivity specificity prospective' returned nothing. No diagnostic-accuracy study of a new regurgitant murmur for endocarditis was sought beyond its Duke-criterion role (unverified recall, no number entered).
